emily_support: Customer (Acme) reports repeated SSE disconnects mid-stream when switching from LTE -> WiFi. Partial last event arrives then connection closes. Repro on iOS 16 (App 5.3.1) and Android 13 (Build 4.9). Raising for triage.

customer_jd: Repro steps we followed: 1) Start SSE stream on mobile over LTE. 2) Turn WiFi on and connect to home AP. 3) ~2-5s after interface change the SSE stream yields a partial JSON event then the client sees a socket error (iOS: -1005 / Android: ECONNRESET). Attached short client log: 
```
2026-03-15T12:10:23.120Z SSE: data: {"id":"abc","delta":"...\n2026-03-15T12:10:23.121Z SSE: parse error: unexpected EOF
2026-03-15T12:10:23.122Z NSURLSession error -1005 connection lost
```
No token rotation at exact moment. We refresh tokens every 10m (TTL 15m) but refresh is not triggered.

raj_engineer: Thanks. Can you confirm which client library you use for SSE and whether you have any app-level reconnection/backoff? Also paste request headers (Authorization, Connection, Accept).

customer_jd: Using our in-house SSE wrapper on top of NSURLSession (iOS) and OkHttp (Android). App uses immediate reconnect (we'll tighten it). Request headers: `Accept: text/event-stream`, `Connection: keep-alive`, `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. No explicit socket keepalive configured in app.

marta_oncall: Infra traces show the TCP connection from their client IP closes within 1s of the interface change. Proxy (edge) logs show: `upstream prematurely closed connection while reading response header from upstream` and a flurry of 502s from same IP range during the window. I also see short-lived spike in RSTs for that client.

raj_engineer: Two likely classes of failure here: (A) client OS tears down socket on interface handoff (common on mobile) causing an RST or abrupt close, (B) NAT/pinhole idle/translation expiry combined with the TCP rebind during handoff producing partial packet delivery. Secondary: poorly-behaved token refresh or background task could start a new request that cancels the streaming request.

emily_support: Customer attached more logs: iOS stack: `NSURLSessionStreamTask: connection lost - code -1005`; their SSE parser shows `data:` line truncated then handler sees stream-closed. They tried adding a 5s app-side comment heartbeat and saw disconnects reduce but not eliminate.

raj_engineer: Recommended immediate triage steps for the customer (and steps we can help with):
1) Server-side heartbeat: emit a lightweight SSE comment or ping (`: keepalive\n\n`) every 15s to keep NAT pinholes alive.
2) Client socket keepalive: configure TCP keepalive on underlying socket (where possible) and increase read timeout to tolerate transient handoffs.
3) Reconnection strategy: on client detect network change, attempt fast reconnect with jittered backoff (avoid immediate aggressive storms). Resume semantics: use idempotent prompts or session IDs so partials are deduplicated.
4) Proxy settings: if you have an intermediate proxy (nginx/varnish) ensure `proxy_buffering off`, `proxy_read_timeout` >> 60s and `send_timeout` is high; for chunked/SSE ensure `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` passes through.
5) Token handling: verify token refresh doesn't spawn a parallel request that cancels the original stream. If refresh required mid-stream, prefer rotating token via a background refresh without aborting the current connection, or issue long-lived session tokens for streaming.
6) Capture pcap/tcpdump during repro to see whether we get FIN vs RST and where packet loss occurs.

eng_runtime_bot: Quick server-side findings for this thread: route `/v1/stream` for Acme on Dedicated showed `keepalive idled` metrics at 10s (lower than default). Edge kept alive 10s then closed idle sockets; recommend bump to 60s for mobile-heavy customers. Also can enable per-route SSE heartbeat at 15s — requires manual toggle for Dedicated accounts.

marta_oncall: Important to differentiate FIN vs RST in capture: FIN = orderly close (maybe proxy timeout), RST = abrupt termination (OS or app kill). If we see TCP retransmits followed by RST, it's likely client OS abort during interface change.

customer_jd: We'll collect tcpdump on Android and a sysdiagnose from iOS run. Quick ask: can Redwood enable per-route heartbeat for our Dedicated tenant while we repro? That would help rule out NAT/pinhole expiry.

raj_engineer: I can enable `sse_heartbeat=15s` for Acme on Dedicated temporarily. I'll log the config change and monitor. In parallel, please attach a minimal reproducible app that we can run in our lab to try handoff. Also confirm whether you're behind a carrier proxy/transparent middlebox.

emily_support: Action items: (1) customer to upload pcap + minimal repro app, (2) raj to enable `sse_heartbeat=15s` on route and bump edge keepalive for that tenant, (3) marta to inspect edge proxy timeouts and confirm `proxy_buffering off` for SSE route. We'll follow up in this thread once captures are in. :thumbsup:

customer_jd: Thanks — will send captures today. Appreciate the quick help.

raj_engineer: If captures show RST from client right at handoff then root cause is client/OS. If FIN after ~10-30s and edge closed the conn then it's proxy/keepalive. Either way we'll add instrumentation to make this easier to diagnose next time (packet-level markers in traces).

marta_oncall: Noted. I'll also add a temporary debug-level edge trace for that tenant while the repro is ongoing.

emily_support: Closing the loop: Raj will update once heartbeat toggle is in place, Marta will share any proxy changes, customer will attach captures. Thanks everyone.
